newsitem.title: UK: California best model for UK Labour, think-tank says.
newsitem.headline: California best model for UK Labour, think-tank says.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government should look to California, with its dynamic, high-tech economy, rather than to continental Europe or Japan, as its economic role model, according to a leading think-tank which has close ties with Prime Minister Tony Blair.
"California offers the most exciting model of economic development for a Blair government," the organisation, Demos, said in a report published on Monday.

Author Charles Leadbeater said countries which Labour thinkers have traditionally looked to, such as Scandinavia, Germany, Japan or the so-called "tiger" economies of south-east Asia, pointed to the past, not the future.

"California already has much of the high-tech economic base that other countries are still striving to create," he wrote. "That is why the Californian model of the knowledge-intensive, networked economy is worth closer scrutiny."

Demos has direct input into the thinking of the Labour government which won a landslide election victory on May 1. Its director, Geoff Mulgan, works for Blair's Downing Street policy unit several days a week.

Leadbeater singled out four key ingredients of California's success: entrepreneurship in knowledge-intensive industries, the development of mutually supportive networks between companies, suppliers and financial backers, a cultural environment which appealed to creative workers and "a distinctively ethical" approach to business.

He said there were similarities between Britain and California in "scale, trading base, culture and outlook," and the two shared problems such as high unemployment, an under-achieving state education system and inadequate transport. Both endured a long recession in the early 1990s but had since shown steady economic growth, although many traditional industries had been lost.

"California's economy has recovered because it has shifted its economic base out of those traditional sectors and into new growth industries which will sustain the economy into the 21st century," Leadbeater said.

"It is at the forefront of the new economy in which soft assets such as knowledge and ideas, creativity and branding will play a far more important role in generating growth than the physical assets of land, manual labour and machinery."

The report concluded that Britain should develop its position in the most "knowledge-intensive" high-growth industries such as biotechnology, software, Internet products, entertainment and communications and financial services.

The Labour government should nurture a political and social climate which was attractive to creative people, promote entrepreneurship and encourage more employees to take stakes in their own companies, it said.
